newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane soars on API data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane soars on API data.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices soared in late trade on Friday upon the release of industry stock data that showed lacklustre builds, traders said.
In the American Petroleum Institute report released late Friday, propane rose about 2.5 million barrels last month to a current total of about 49.46 million barrels, players said.
The build was mostly at the expense of the U.S. Gulf Coast, which showed an unexpected 137,000-barrel draw. The Conway, Kansas hub in the Midwest had a 1.4 million barrel build, traders said.
"The numbers are very bullish," said one Houston trader.
Soon after the data's release, Mont Belvieu, Texas, shot up about one cent to between 49.50 cents and 49.75 cents a gallon. A deal was reported done at 49.50 cents in what was still slow activity.
Conway, Kansas, hub material, however, soared about 1.50 cents to 49.25/49.50 cents. 49.25-cent and 49.50-cent parcels were traded in moderate dealings, players said.
Players also expressed concern over a 483,000 barrel draw on ethane since a one million barrel build was expected by many traders.
Total U.S. ethane stocks as of Aug. 31 stood at 16.89 million, 13.6 million barrels below levels last year.
"People are still digesting the numbers, but I expect Monday is going to open up very strong," said one Houston trader.
-- Laney Salisbury New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
